analysis.title: Thomson Reuters Corp. (TRI): 3Q revenue upside offset by softer near-term organic growth and margin outlook
key_insights: GS reiterates Buy on TRI and raises the 12-month price target from $125 to $130 (C$173 to C$182 for TRI.TO). Price was $122.24, implying 6.3% upside.
3Q 2026 revenue was $1,833mn, up 10.6% y/y, above GS estimate of 8.7% growth and FactSet consensus of 10.1%. Organic growth was 10% vs GS forecast of 8.9% and 9% in 2Q.
Big 3 organic revenue grew 10% in 3Q, above GS estimate of 9.5% and in line with 2Q. The company reaffirmed its 2026 Big 3 organic growth outlook of 9.5-10.0% and its Big 3 margin outlook.

Adjusted EBITDA margin contracted 30 bps y/y to 35.5% on higher Legal investment, but beat GS forecast of 34.6% and was in line with consensus. Big 3 EBITDA margin fell about 110 bps y/y to 40.3% on severance, automation and innovation investment, and bolt-on M&A dilution.
Adjusted EPS of $0.81 beat GS estimate of $0.77 but slightly missed consensus of $0.83.

Legal organic growth was 9% y/y vs 10% in 2Q. Government grew 4% and international was slightly softer, while US law-firm sub-segments stayed at or near record growth. Legal excluding government was only 20 bps below 2Q.

Gen AI-enabled products reached 34% of ACV vs 30% in 2Q and 24% a year ago, supported by Westlaw Advantage and CoCounsel. Next-generation CoCounsel Legal shows stronger engagement, retention and NPS than the prior version.

The Global Print divestiture removes a structurally declining business and adds 60-70 bps to organic growth. It cut reported 2026 EBITDA margin guidance from about 40% to about 39% through discontinued-operations accounting. Royalty and transition services reimbursements should offset stranded costs from 4Q 2026. Proceeds were $500mn.

Company guides 4Q organic growth to about 8%, down from 10% in 3Q, on a roughly 150 bps lower Reuters contribution and moderating Corporate transactional revenue. Reuters should be about flat y/y after lapping $5mn of AI licensing revenue, tougher agency comparisons and a cancelled Middle East event.

TRI said it could have reached about 41% 2027 EBITDA margin under its prior reporting structure before incremental investment, but plans to reinvest part of that operating leverage in AI-related growth, limiting near-term margin expansion.

2026 guidance: reported revenue growth raised from about 8.0% to about 9.5%, organic growth from about 8% to 8.5-9.0%, EBITDA margin lowered from 40%+ to about 39%, FCF about $2.1bn unchanged. 4Q EBITDA margin guided to about 42%.

GS cuts 2026/2027/2028 EBITDA margin forecasts from 39.2%/41.2%/42.2% to 39.0%/40.1%/40.7% on AI and growth investment. EPS estimates move from $3.96/$4.74/$5.48 to $3.95/$4.63/$5.30. 2026 revenue estimate rises from $7,660mn to $7,674mn.

Target price rests on 25.5x (24.5x prior) rolled-forward NTM+1YR EPS of $5.11, above the 17.5x median Info Services NTM P/E, on resilient growth, competitive moat and execution record. The multiple was raised to reflect peer multiple appreciation.
Stock is up 24.6% over 3 months and 27.5% over 6 months but down 21.4% over 12 months in absolute terms.

market_movers.rationale: Target raised from $125 to $130 on a higher target multiple. Big 3 growth, improving mix and AI monetization support long-term earnings growth, while 4Q deceleration and 2027 reinvestment temper near-term earnings.

earnings_insights: TRI 3Q 2026 (reported 11/3): revenue $1,833mn, +10.6% y/y, vs GS estimate $1,803mn (8.7% growth per text) and FactSet consensus growth of 10.1%.
TRI 3Q 2026 adjusted EPS $0.81 reported vs GS estimate $0.77 and FactSet consensus $0.83. Reported diluted EPS $0.78 vs GS estimate $0.87.
TRI 3Q 2026 adjusted EBITDA $651mn vs GS estimate $623mn, margin 35.5% vs GS 34.6%, in line with consensus.
TRI 4Q 2026 guide: organic revenue growth about 8%, EBITDA margin about 42%. GS 4Q 2026E adjusted EPS cut from $1.22 to $1.17 and revenue from $2,038.8mn to $2,022.6mn.

GS FY2026E adjusted EPS $3.95, FY2027E $4.63, FY2028E $5.30. GS prior to the print forecast 2026 reported revenue growth of 9.6% vs FactSet consensus 12.4%, and guidance points to negative consensus revisions for revenue and stable EBITDA margin estimates.
risk_factors: Macro headwinds that could pressure customer budgets.
Slower-than-expected customer adoption of AI-enabled products.
Elevated investment spending causing an EBITDA margin shortfall.

tension_points.bull_case: Big 3 organic growth held at 10% for a second quarter, Gen AI products reached 34% of ACV, and Legal remains strong with Westlaw Advantage and CoCounsel driving upgrades. Global Print divestiture adds 60-70 bps to organic growth.
tension_points.bear_case: 4Q organic growth is guided to about 8% on Reuters comparisons and Corporate transactional moderation. 2027 operating leverage is partly reinvested in AI, so GS cuts 2027 EBITDA margin to 40.1% from 41.2% and 2027 EPS to $4.63 from $4.74.
tension_points.what_invalidates: An EBITDA margin shortfall from elevated investment spending, or slower customer adoption of AI-enabled products, would weaken the bull case.
